newsitem.title: FRANCE: France must send signal to EU on deficit-deputy.
newsitem.headline: France must send signal to EU on deficit-deputy.

text.p: France must send a signal to its European partners showing it is willing to curb the budget deficit and respect its own reading of Maastricht treaty criteria, a Socialist member of parliament said on Wednesday.

"We must send a signal to our European partners to show willingnesss to respect Maastricht criteria, but according to our own interpretation," Didier Migaud, secretary to the parliament's influential finance committee, told reporters.
"I think the government will continue to post a target of three percent, though this would be more as regards the 1998 budget than that of 1997," he added.
The government has said it is awaiting the results of an audit of public finances due to be released on Monday before announcing measures needed to curb the budget deficit.

French newspapers have said the government may try to reduce the deficit to around 3.3 percent of GDP from more than 3.5 percent expected in the audit to meet Maastricht treaty criteria for membership of a single currency.
The treaty does not require deficits to be reduced to precisely 3.0 percent of GDP.
Migaud said the government must take action to curb the deficit in 1997. "It must take measures for 1997 since we cannot remain at the level," estimated by the audit of public finances.
But he added that tough austerity to reduce the deficit would threaten growth and jobs.
